systemPrompt:
You are an expert at planning interactive 3D visualizations for textbook figures.

PRIMARY CONTEXT:
The generated figure will be embedded alongside the original in a PDF reader. It should look recognizably like the source figure — same general geometry, viewpoint, labels, and proportions — but does not need to be a pixel-perfect inline replacement. Some additional controls or layout breathing room are fine if they genuinely help the learner.

INTERACTION PALETTE — choose the interactions that best fit the concept. Pick the fewest that genuinely serve the learning goal; more is not better. In "teaches", say what the learner understands, not what the control does.

• orbit / drag — rotate/move the scene. When depth or 3D shape IS the concept.
• hover — reveal a label on demand. When showing every label at once clutters.
• click — highlight one element. When focus on one part of a busy scene matters.
• slider — sweep one continuous variable. When dragging it visibly transforms the figure.
• toggle — switch between 2+ named views. For before/after or dual views (e.g. spatial ↔ frequency).
• button / state — step through discrete phases. When distinct stages should be visited deliberately.
• animation — self-playing motion. When the concept is inherently dynamic and a slider can't convey it.
• equation_input — learner types math, parsed at runtime. When "change the formula, reshape the output" (integrand, boundary, kernel); each field maps to one curve/quantity; catch parse errors inline.
• code_editor — learner writes/debugs an algorithm; the figure replays its execution frame by frame. Use ONLY when the concept IS a procedure whose intermediate states carry the lesson — heapify, one pass of a sort, a graph traversal, gradient descent, scanline fill — i.e. the question a learner has is "in what order does it touch the data, and why". Needs state small enough to draw whole (~30 elements) and an algorithm expressible in ~20 lines against a handful of operations. Do NOT use it for a continuous parameter (that is a slider), a formula the learner retypes (equation_input), or a static structure with no execution (hover/click). Choose it over animation when the learner should be able to get the procedure WRONG and watch where it diverges.

Output ONLY valid JSON (no markdown, no explanation):
{
  "projection_type": "perspective | axonometric | oblique",
  "camera_view": { "azimuthDeg": <perspective only — 0=side · 45=three-quarter · 90=front-on>, "elevationDeg": <perspective only — 0=eye-level · 20-35=slightly above · 90=top-down>, "rollDeg": 0, "heightFraction": <0.5 default · up to 0.75 to fill the frame> },
  "axis_screen_angles": <axonometric only — null for a flat 2D plot/diagram with no 3D depth (front-on view); omit this field entirely for a 3D axonometric figure (renderer uses a standard isometric pose)>,
  "elements": ["exhaustive list of every geometric element visible in the figure that must be recreated in 3D"],
  "interactions": [
    { "id": "uniqueCamelCaseId", "type": "orbit | drag | hover | click | slider | toggle | button | state | animation | equation_input | code_editor", "teaches": "what the learner understands", "...": "plus ONLY that type's fields — see INTERACTION FIELDS below" }
  ],
  "demo_steps": [
    {
      "title": "Step name shown in UI",
      "narration": "What the learner sees and understands at this step — one or two sentences",
      "state": { "interactionId": value }
    }
  ],
  "geometry_notes": "Approximate world-space scale (e.g. 'cube ~2 units side, axes span ±3'), dominant colors from the source, and any domain-specific formula or value needed for correctness.",
  "notes": "Three.js / rendering technique notes (distinct from geometry_notes)"
}

INTERACTION FIELDS — every interaction object has "id" (unique camelCase), "type", and "teaches". Add ONLY the fields listed for its type; never attach a "range" to anything but a slider.

"type" MUST be exactly one of these 11 strings: "orbit" · "drag" · "hover" · "click" · "slider" · "toggle" · "button" · "state" · "animation" · "equation_input" · "code_editor""

• orbit / drag / hover / click — no extra fields.
• animation      — "label", optional "loop": true | false.
• slider         — "label", "range": [min, max, step], "default": <number>.
• toggle         — "label", "options": ["A", "B", ...], "default": "A"   (a plain on/off toggle may drop "options" and use "default": true | false).
• button / state — "label", "states": ["idle", "running", "done"], "default": "idle".
• equation_input — "label", "fields": [ { "id": "...", "label": "f(x) =", "default": "sin(x)", "variables": ["x"], "domain": [min, max], "role": "integrand | boundary | kernel | ..." } ]. "domain" is the x-range the field is plotted over; always supply it so the generator does not have to guess.
• code_editor    — "label",
                   "entry_point": "the one function the learner must define, e.g. buildMaxHeap(heap)",
                   "api": [ { "op": "greater(i, j)", "does": "true when A[i] > A[j]" }, { "op": "swap(i, j)", "does": "exchange two elements — the ONLY way to mutate" }, ... ],
                   "frame": "what one recorded step shows, e.g. 'the whole array plus the 1-2 indices the op touched'",
                   "input": { "label": "Initial array", "default": "4, 1, 3, 2, 16, 9, 10" },
                   "sample_code": "<correct implementation, as a string>",
                   optional "buggy_code": "<plausible near-miss, with a comment naming the bug>",
                   "success_check": "the property the final state must satisfy, e.g. 'every parent >= both of its children'".
  Design the "api" first and keep it minimal: 4–7 ops covering read, compare, mutate, and annotate (a note/mark op for the learner's own commentary). Every state change must be reachable ONLY through an op — otherwise the replay has gaps. The learner writes algorithm logic, never drawing code.

demo_steps "state" may set values for slider, toggle, and button/state interactions only; code_editor and equation_input are seeded by their sample_code / fields defaults, not by demo_steps.

Rules:
- PROJECTION TYPE: pick whichever the source most resembles. Do not measure angles off the image — the renderer applies a fixed standard pose for each type, so a coarse visual call is enough. Spend your effort on ELEMENTS and INTERACTIONS instead; camera is a quick classification, not a measurement task.
  • "perspective" — depth edges clearly converge toward a vanishing point, or a single object's own far end reads smaller than its near end. Judge within one object; a row of separate same-shape objects that merely shrink (e.g. neural-net layers) is not perspective.
  • "oblique" — one face is drawn true (an undistorted rectangle: right angles, horizontal/vertical edges intact) while depth recedes off it along a single diagonal — e.g. stacked feature maps/filter banks drawn as offset same-size copies.
  • "axonometric" — the default for everything else: any other 3D-looking figure (axes tilted, no true face), or a flat 2D plot/diagram (set "axis_screen_angles": null for these).
- CAMERA VIEW: camera_view sets framing only. azimuthDeg/elevationDeg apply to perspective only: azimuthDeg 0 side, 45 three-quarter, 90 front-on; elevationDeg 0 eye-level, 10–20 low-angle, 25–35 moderate three-quarter, 90 top-down. rollDeg is usually 0. heightFraction is how much of the frame the figure should fill (0.5 default, up to 0.75).
- DEMO STEPS: include when the concept has 2+ distinct phases the learner should visit in sequence, each step driving one named configuration of the interaction state. Use [] for a single continuous exploration with no natural sequence.
- GEOMETRY NOTES: always fill this in — it is what stops the generator guessing sizes and getting the zoom wrong. Cover:
  • world-space dimensions, and for oblique/axonometric figures give each box explicitly as X × Y × Z world units, naming which source dimension each axis carries (+X is screen-right, +Y screen-up, +Z the receding diagonal).
  • the colour palette, with hex codes where determinable from the source.
  • any formula or numeric range the generator needs to be mathematically correct.
  • POSITION AND ORIENTATION for each element as read off the source — which way it points, what angle it sits at, which side of another element it is on. Read this off the image; do not infer layout from general knowledge of the concept. A generic, plausible-looking arrangement is the failure mode the generator falls into whenever geometry_notes covers only dimensions.
  • for a repeated shape with a stated per-element value (channel count, layer size, category), an explicit number for each element's varying dimension tied to that value — equal values get equal size, even across sequence position — rather than a described trend.
- MULTI-PART FIGURES: if the source contains multiple labeled panels ((a)/(b)/(c), side-by-side comparisons, before/after pairs, sequential diagrams), do NOT recreate them all simultaneously in the initial view. Show one panel by default and link the rest through a single interaction — a toggle, tab, or slider — so the learner actively moves between parts. The transition itself should teach the comparison or progression.
- Prefer interactions that expose relationships in the figure rather than generic controls.

Here are two examples of good plans:

=== EXAMPLE 1: Geometric 3D scene with sliders driving continuous object motion ===

Textbook context:
Perspective projection derived geometrically. A 3D point P at (X, Y, Z) projects through the pinhole at the origin onto the projection plane at distance f. From similar triangles: x = f * X/Z and y = f * Y/Z, so distant objects become smaller through the inverse scaling by Z.

      "label": "Depth Z",
      "range": [2, 12, 0.5],

    {

      "narration": "P at depth Z=5 projects through the pinhole to x=f·X/Z=0.8 on the plane. Observe the ray from P through the origin continuing to the projected point.",

    }
  ],
  "geometry_notes": "Pinhole at origin: SphereGeometry ~0.08 units radius, black. 3D point P at roughly (2, 0.5, -5) from origin. Projection plane at z=-f as semi-transparent PlaneGeometry ~3×2 units, blue 0.18 opacity. Ray as a thin Line from P through origin to projected point. Geometry fits within ±3 X, ±2 Y, -12 to 0 Z. Colors: pinhole black, P orange #ff8800, projected point red #cc2200, ray red, plane blue.",

}

=== EXAMPLE 2: Mathematical function figure with a slider and a domain toggle ===

Textbook context:
The parameter sigma adjusts the spatial extent of the Gaussian g(x; sigma) = (1 / sqrt(2*pi*sigma^2)) * exp(-x^2 / (2*sigma^2)), normalized to integrate to 1. In practice only samples within three standard deviations are needed. The Fourier transform of a Gaussian is also a Gaussian, with width inversely proportional to sigma.

}

Figure: geometry_reconstruction_12

AUTHOR-PROVIDED INTERACTION REQUESTS:
Requested interactions:
- Live two-view model: the back-projected ray P = zK⁻¹p, the rigid transform P' = MP, and the reprojection p' = KP are recomputed continuously from the current geometry
- Slider for depth z along the ray through p: the 3D point slides along the ray and both image projections update together, showing the depth ambiguity a single view leaves
- Sliders for the relative pose (R, T) of the second camera: watch p' move in the reference frame while p stays fixed, visualizing how motion parameters determine where the correspondence lands

Source file:
visionbook/3d_learning.qmd

Use these requested interactions when forming the plan. Use the image to recover visual structure, layout, labels, camera/view cues, and missing visible elements.

Planner context:
This figure illustrates the two-frame geometry of 3D point reconstruction from a moving camera. Two image planes are shown — a reference frame and a target frame — with a 3D point P visible from both; the image point p on the target frame is lifted back to 3D via P = zK⁻¹p using the intrinsic calibration matrix K and depth z. The two camera frames are related by an extrinsic rigid-body transformation parameterized by rotation R and translation T (the loop P' = MP at the 3D point), and the transformed point is projected onto the reference frame as p' = KP. This figure sets up the two-view reconstruction pipeline in which known or estimated camera motion and intrinsic calibration K together determine the 3D location of a scene point from its projected image correspondences across frames.

CONTEXT FROM TEXTBOOK:
This figure illustrates the two-frame geometry of 3D point reconstruction from a moving camera. Two image planes are shown — a reference frame and a target frame — with a 3D point P visible from both; the image point p on the target frame is lifted back to 3D via P = zK⁻¹p using the intrinsic calibration matrix K and depth z. The two camera frames are related by an extrinsic rigid-body transformation parameterized by rotation R and translation T (the loop P' = MP at the 3D point), and the transformed point is projected onto the reference frame as p' = KP. This figure sets up the two-view reconstruction pipeline in which known or estimated camera motion and intrinsic calibration K together determine the 3D location of a scene point from its projected image correspondences across frames.

PROJECTION TYPE: perspective
Use the scaffold's true perspective projection after building all geometry. Use this only when the source has real vanishing-point convergence or distance-based size shrinkage; then depth should visibly affect apparent size.

ELEMENTS TO RECREATE IN 3D:
  - target image plane ℓ₂: thin rectangular quad on the left, tilted so its face angles toward the scene
  - reference image plane ℓ₁: thin rectangular quad on the right, tilted similarly
  - target camera center C₂: small black sphere below/behind ℓ₂
  - reference camera center C₁: small black sphere below/behind ℓ₁
  - 3D scene point P: red sphere floating above and between the two planes
  - image point p: red dot on the target plane ℓ₂
  - image point p': red dot on the reference plane ℓ₁
  - dashed back-projection ray from C₂ through p continuing up to P
  - dashed projection ray from C₁ through p' continuing up to P
  - curved gray arrow from p up to P labeled P = zK⁻¹p
  - curved gray self-loop arrow at P labeled P' = MP
  - curved gray arrow from P down to p' labeled p' = KP
  - curved gray baseline arrow from C₂ to C₁ labeled R, T
  - text labels: ℓ₂, ℓ₁, p, p', P, 'Target frame', 'Reference frame'

GEOMETRY NOTES (world-space scale, color palette, and any formula/value needed for correctness — build to these so sizes, zoom, and colors match the source; do not guess dimensions the notes already specify):
World scale: target camera center C₂ at (-2.2, 0, 0), reference camera center C₁ at (2.2, 0, 0). Each image plane is a ~1.3 (wide) × 1.0 (tall) unit quad placed ~1.0 unit in front of its camera center and tilted ~25° so its face angles toward the central scene region (matching the source's leaning parallelograms). 3D point P near (0, 1.6, 4). Intrinsic K simplified to focal f=2, principal point at plane center. Back-projection: in target-camera coords P = z·(px/f, py/f, 1); reference-frame point P_ref = R·P + T with R a rotation about the vertical (Y) axis by rotY and T = (transX, 0, 0); reprojection p' = (f·P_ref.x/P_ref.z, f·P_ref.y/P_ref.z). Colors: plane edges black #111111 with near-transparent white fill; P, p, p' red #cc1111; camera centers black #111111; dashed sight-lines black; pipeline arrows and R,T baseline arrow gray #999999; all equation/frame text black. Everything fits within roughly X ∈ [-3.5, 3.5], Y ∈ [-0.5, 2.5], Z ∈ [0, 8].

DISCRETE CONTROLS (implement every one of these in #ui, each must work independently):
[
  {
    "id": "orbit",
    "type": "orbit",
    "teaches": "Rotating the scene reveals that the two image planes, the two camera centers, and P all live in one 3D space, and that each dashed line is a true sight-line from a camera center through its image point to the same 3D point"
  },
  {
    "id": "depthZ",
    "type": "slider",
    "label": "Depth z along ray",
    "range": [
      1.5,
      8,
      0.1
    ],
    "default": 4,
    "teaches": "Sliding P along the fixed back-projection ray through p leaves p unchanged but moves p' on the reference plane — a single view cannot fix depth, only the second view's geometry resolves it"
  },
  {
    "id": "rotY",
    "type": "slider",
    "label": "Relative rotation R (about vertical)",
    "range": [
      -45,
      45,
      1
    ],
    "default": 0,
    "teaches": "Rotating the reference camera swings the sight-line to P, dragging p' across ℓ₁ while p stays put — rotation alone changes where the correspondence lands"
  },
  {
    "id": "transX",
    "type": "slider",
    "label": "Relative translation T (baseline)",
    "range": [
      -2,
      2,
      0.05
    ],
    "default": 0,
    "teaches": "Translating the reference camera shifts the parallax of P, moving p' along the epipolar direction — translation provides the baseline that makes depth observable"
  }
]

DEMO STEPS (tween through these using goToStep(); each step drives the controls above):
[
  {
    "title": "Two-view setup",
    "narration": "P is back-projected from p via P = zK⁻¹p, rigidly transformed by the relative pose (P' = MP), and reprojected to p' = KP on the reference plane. Both dashed sight-lines meet at the same 3D point.",
    "state": {
      "depthZ": 4,
      "rotY": 0,
      "transX": 0
    }
  },
  {
    "title": "Depth ambiguity",
    "narration": "Increase z to 7. P slides farther out along the ray through p; p does not move, but p' shifts on ℓ₁. One image leaves depth free — the second view is what pins it down.",
    "state": {
      "depthZ": 7,
      "rotY": 0,
      "transX": 0
    }
  },
  {
    "title": "Pose drives correspondence",
    "narration": "Rotate the reference camera by 25° and translate the baseline by 1. p stays fixed on ℓ₂ while p' sweeps across ℓ₁, showing how R and T determine the matching location.",
    "state": {
      "depthZ": 4,
      "rotY": 25,
      "transX": 1
    }
  }
]

CAMERA VIEW (framing only). Call setCameraView({ projection, ...these }) AFTER all geometry is added. Keep the projection MECHANISM from PROJECTION TYPE above (orthographic / sheared-oblique / perspective). For perspective these params set the pose (azimuth/elevation/roll); for the two parallel projections pose is a standard default (see PROJECTION TYPE above), and these params set only roll and framing (heightFraction):
{
  "azimuthDeg": 32,
  "elevationDeg": 16,
  "rollDeg": 0,
  "heightFraction": 0.68
}

NOTES: Build the two cameras as real pinhole models with THREE.Matrix4 for K, R, T so P, p, p' recompute reactively on every slider change. Represent dashed sight-lines as LineDashedMaterial (call computeLineDistances). Render p and p' as small spheres parented to their image-plane quads so they sit exactly on the plane surface; recompute p' position each frame from the projection math and clamp/hide it if P_ref.z <= 0 (point behind reference camera). Equation labels (P=zK⁻¹p, P'=MP, p'=KP, R,T) and frame names are static sprites/HTML overlays positioned near their arrows; the curved arrows can be static TubeGeometry/QuadraticBezier curves since only the points and rays move. Keep both planes' geometry static; only P, the two red image dots, and the two dashed rays update.

Follow the interaction plan above.

function computeBasis(camPos, target) {
  const Z = target.clone().sub(camPos).normalize();
  const up = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0);
  const X = new THREE.Vector3().crossVectors(up, Z).normalize();
  const Y = new THREE.Vector3().crossVectors(Z, X).normalize();
  return { X, Y, Z };
}

const cam2 = computeBasis(C2, lookTarget);
const cam1 = computeBasis(C1, lookTarget);

const p_img = { x: 0.3, y: 0.6 };

const grayMat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0x999999 });

const dashMat = new THREE.LineDashedMaterial({ color: 0x111111, dashSize: 0.12, gapSize: 0.08 });

  const line = new THREE.LineSegments(edges, planeEdgeMat);
  group.add(line);
  const m = new THREE.Matrix4().makeBasis(camBasis.X, camBasis.Y, camBasis.Z);

scene.add(pPrimeDot);

const ray1Geom = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
const ray1 = new THREE.Line(ray1Geom, dashMat);
scene.add(ray1);

// ── Curved arrows (static) ──
function createArrowTube(start, end, ctrl, radius) {
  const curve = new THREE.QuadraticBezierCurve3(start, ctrl, end);
  const tubeGeom = new THREE.TubeGeometry(curve, 32, radius || 0.02, 8, false);
  const tube = new THREE.Mesh(tubeGeom, grayMat);
  scene.add(tube);
  const tangent = curve.getTangent(1).normalize();
  const cone = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.ConeGeometry(0.05, 0.14, 8), grayMat);
  cone.position.copy(end);
  cone.quaternion.setFromUnitVectors(new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0), tangent);
  scene.add(cone);
  return { tube, cone };
}

// Default positions for arrow placement
const pWorld_default = C2.clone()
  .add(cam2.X.clone().multiplyScalar(p_img.x / f))
  .add(cam2.Y.clone().multiplyScalar(p_img.y / f))
  .add(cam2.Z.clone().multiplyScalar(1.0));

const P_default = C2.clone()
  .add(cam2.X.clone().multiplyScalar(4 * p_img.x / f))
  .add(cam2.Y.clone().multiplyScalar(4 * p_img.y / f))
  .add(cam2.Z.clone().multiplyScalar(4));

// Arrow p→P
const arrow1Ctrl = new THREE.Vector3(
  pWorld_default.x - 0.8,
  (pWorld_default.y + P_default.y) / 2 + 0.6,
  (pWorld_default.z + P_default.z) / 2
);
createArrowTube(pWorld_default.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.08, 0)), P_default.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(-0.1, -0.05, 0)), arrow1Ctrl, 0.02);

// Arrow P→p'
const pPrime_default_pos = new THREE.Vector3(1.64, 0.40, 0.80);
const arrow2Ctrl = new THREE.Vector3(
  (P_default.x + pPrime_default_pos.x) / 2 + 0.8,
  (P_default.y + pPrime_default_pos.y) / 2 + 0.4,
  (P_default.z + pPrime_default_pos.z) / 2
);
createArrowTube(P_default.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0.1, -0.05, 0)), pPrime_default_pos.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.08, 0)), arrow2Ctrl, 0.02);

// Self-loop at P
const loopCenter = P_default.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0.15, 0.35, 0));
const loopRadius = 0.28;
const loopPts = [];
for (let i = 0; i <= 40; i++) {
  const angle = -Math.PI * 0.7 + (i / 40) * Math.PI * 1.8;
  loopPts.push(new THREE.Vector3(
    loopCenter.x + loopRadius * Math.cos(angle),
    loopCenter.y + loopRadius * Math.sin(angle),
    loopCenter.z
  ));
}
const loopCurve = new THREE.CatmullRomCurve3(loopPts);
const loopTube = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.TubeGeometry(loopCurve, 40, 0.02, 8, false), grayMat);
scene.add(loopTube);
const loopEnd = loopPts[loopPts.length - 1];
const loopTangent = loopPts[loopPts.length - 1].clone().sub(loopPts[loopPts.length - 2]).normalize();
const loopCone = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.ConeGeometry(0.05, 0.14, 8), grayMat);
loopCone.position.copy(loopEnd);
loopCone.quaternion.setFromUnitVectors(new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0), loopTangent);
scene.add(loopCone);

// Baseline arrow C₂→C₁
const baseCtrl = new THREE.Vector3(0, -0.9, 0);
createArrowTube(C2.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0.1, -0.1, 0)), C1.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(-0.1, -0.1, 0)), baseCtrl, 0.02);

// ── Update function ──
const depthSlider = document.getElementById('depthZ');
const rotSlider = document.getElementById('rotY');
const transSlider = document.getElementById('transX');

function updateScene() {
  const z = parseFloat(depthSlider.value);
  const rotYDeg = parseFloat(rotSlider.value);
  const transXVal = parseFloat(transSlider.value);
  const rotYRad = rotYDeg * Math.PI / 180;

  // Back-project p to get P in target camera coords
  const P_cam2 = new THREE.Vector3(z * p_img.x / f, z * p_img.y / f, z);

  // P in world coords
  const P_world = C2.clone()
    .add(cam2.X.clone().multiplyScalar(P_cam2.x))
    .add(cam2.Y.clone().multiplyScalar(P_cam2.y))
    .add(cam2.Z.clone().multiplyScalar(P_cam2.z));

  // p on target plane (fixed)
  const p_on_plane = C2.clone()
    .add(cam2.X.clone().multiplyScalar(p_img.x / f))
    .add(cam2.Y.clone().multiplyScalar(p_img.y / f))
    .add(cam2.Z.clone().multiplyScalar(1.0));

  // Modified reference camera
  const cosR = Math.cos(rotYRad), sinR = Math.sin(rotYRad);
  const C1_mod = C1.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(transXVal, 0, 0));
  const X1_mod = new THREE.Vector3(
    cam1.X.x * cosR + cam1.X.z * sinR,
    cam1.X.y,
    -cam1.X.x * sinR + cam1.X.z * cosR
  );
  const Y1_mod = new THREE.Vector3(
    cam1.Y.x * cosR + cam1.Y.z * sinR,
    cam1.Y.y,
    -cam1.Y.x * sinR + cam1.Y.z * cosR
  );
  const Z1_mod = new THREE.Vector3(
    cam1.Z.x * cosR + cam1.Z.z * sinR,
    cam1.Z.y,
    -cam1.Z.x * sinR + cam1.Z.z * cosR
  );

  // Project P into modified reference camera
  const P_rel = P_world.clone().sub(C1_mod);
  const P_ref = new THREE.Vector3(
    X1_mod.dot(P_rel),
    Y1_mod.dot(P_rel),
    Z1_mod.dot(P_rel)
  );

  let pPrimeVisible = false;
  let pPrime_world = new THREE.Vector3();

  if (P_ref.z > 0.05) {
    const pPrime_img = { x: f * P_ref.x / P_ref.z, y: f * P_ref.y / P_ref.z };
    // Check if p' is within plane bounds (roughly ±0.65 x, ±0.5 y)
    if (Math.abs(pPrime_img.x) < 1.2 && Math.abs(pPrime_img.y) < 1.0) {
      pPrime_world = C1_mod.clone()
        .add(X1_mod.clone().multiplyScalar(pPrime_img.x / f))
        .add(Y1_mod.clone().multiplyScalar(pPrime_img.y / f))
        .add(Z1_mod.clone().multiplyScalar(1.0));
      pPrimeVisible = true;
    }
  }

  // Update P position
  pMesh.position.copy(P_world);

  // Update p position (fixed)
  pDot.position.copy(p_on_plane);

  // Update p' position
  if (pPrimeVisible) {
    pPrimeDot.visible = true;
    pPrimeDot.position.copy(pPrime_world);
  } else {
    pPrimeDot.visible = false;
  }

  // Update dashed ray from C₂ through p to P
  const ray2Pts = [C2.clone(), p_on_plane.clone(), P_world.clone()];
  ray2.geometry.dispose();
  ray2.geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry().setFromPoints(ray2Pts);
  ray2.computeLineDistances();

  // Update dashed ray from C₁ through p' to P
  if (pPrimeVisible) {
    ray1.visible = true;
    const ray1Pts = [C1_mod.clone(), pPrime_world.clone(), P_world.clone()];
    ray1.geometry.dispose();
    ray1.geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry().setFromPoints(ray1Pts);
    ray1.computeLineDistances();
  } else {
    ray1.visible = false;
  }

  // Update reference plane and camera center positions if translated
  c1Mesh.position.copy(C1_mod);
  const m1 = new THREE.Matrix4().makeBasis(X1_mod, Y1_mod, Z1_mod);
  plane1.quaternion.setFromRotationMatrix(m1);
  plane1.position.copy(C1_mod).add(Z1_mod.clone().multiplyScalar(1.0));
}

function goToStep(idx) {
  const target = steps[idx];

    depthZ: parseFloat(depthSlider.value),
    rotY: parseFloat(rotSlider.value),
    transX: parseFloat(transSlider.value)
  };
  const duration = 800;
  const t0 = performance.now();
  if (tweenId) cancelAnimationFrame(tweenId);
  function tick() {
    const t = Math.min(1, (performance.now() - t0) / duration);
    const ease = t * t * (3 - 2 * t);
    depthSlider.value = start.depthZ + (target.depthZ - start.depthZ) * ease;
    rotSlider.value = start.rotY + (target.rotY - start.rotY) * ease;
    transSlider.value = start.transX + (target.transX - start.transX) * ease;
    updateScene();
    if (t < 1) tweenId = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  }
  tick();
}

const f = 2;
const C2 = new THREE.Vector3(-2.2, 0, 0);
const C1 = new THREE.Vector3(2.2, 0, 0);
const lookTarget = new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.5, 4.5);

function computeBasis(camPos, target) {
  const Z = target.clone().sub(camPos).normalize();
  const up = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0);
  const X = new THREE.Vector3().crossVectors(up, Z).normalize();
  const Y = new THREE.Vector3().crossVectors(Z, X).normalize();
  return { X, Y, Z };
}

const cam2 = computeBasis(C2, lookTarget);
const cam1 = computeBasis(C1, lookTarget);

const p_img = { x: 0.3, y: 0.5 };

// ── Materials ──
const blackMat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0x111111 });
const redMat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0xcc1111 });
const grayMat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0x999999 });
const planeFillMat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0xffffff, transparent: true, opacity: 0.06, side: THREE.DoubleSide });
const planeEdgeMat = new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({ color: 0x111111 });
const dashMat = new THREE.LineDashedMaterial({ color: 0x111111, dashSize: 0.15, gapSize: 0.10 });

// ── Image planes ──
function createPlane(camBasis, camPos) {
  const group = new THREE.Group();
  const geom = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(1.3, 1.0);
  const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geom, planeFillMat);
  group.add(mesh);
  const edges = new THREE.EdgesGeometry(geom);
  const line = new THREE.LineSegments(edges, planeEdgeMat);
  group.add(line);
  const m = new THREE.Matrix4().makeBasis(camBasis.X, camBasis.Y, camBasis.Z);
  group.quaternion.setFromRotationMatrix(m);
  group.position.copy(camPos).add(camBasis.Z.clone().multiplyScalar(1.0));
  scene.add(group);
  return group;
}

const plane2 = createPlane(cam2, C2);
const plane1 = createPlane(cam1, C1);

// ── Camera centers ──
const c2Mesh = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.07, 16, 16), blackMat);
c2Mesh.position.copy(C2);
scene.add(c2Mesh);

const c1Mesh = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.07, 16, 16), blackMat);
c1Mesh.position.copy(C1);
scene.add(c1Mesh);

// ── 3D point P ──
const pMesh = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.09, 16, 16), redMat);
scene.add(pMesh);

// ── Image points p and p' ──
const pDot = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.055, 12, 12), redMat);
scene.add(pDot);

const pPrimeDot = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.055, 12, 12), redMat);
scene.add(pPrimeDot);

// ── Dashed rays ──
const ray2Geom = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
const ray2 = new THREE.Line(ray2Geom, dashMat);
scene.add(ray2);

const ray1Geom = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
const ray1 = new THREE.Line(ray1Geom, dashMat);
scene.add(ray1);

// ── Curved arrows helper ──
function createArrowTube(start, end, ctrl, radius) {
  const curve = new THREE.QuadraticBezierCurve3(start, ctrl, end);
  const tubeGeom = new THREE.TubeGeometry(curve, 32, radius || 0.022, 8, false);
  const tube = new THREE.Mesh(tubeGeom, grayMat);
  scene.add(tube);
  const tangent = curve.getTangent(1).normalize();
  const cone = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.ConeGeometry(0.06, 0.16, 8), grayMat);
  cone.position.copy(end);
  cone.quaternion.setFromUnitVectors(new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0), tangent);
  scene.add(cone);
  return { tube, cone };
}

// Default positions
const pWorld_default = C2.clone()
  .add(cam2.X.clone().multiplyScalar(p_img.x / f))
  .add(cam2.Y.clone().multiplyScalar(p_img.y / f))
  .add(cam2.Z.clone().multiplyScalar(1.0));

const P_default = C2.clone()
  .add(cam2.X.clone().multiplyScalar(4 * p_img.x / f))
  .add(cam2.Y.clone().multiplyScalar(4 * p_img.y / f))
  .add(cam2.Z.clone().multiplyScalar(4));

const pPrime_default_pos = new THREE.Vector3(1.6, 0.35, 0.85);

// Arrow p→P (large sweep from left plane up to P)
const arrow1Ctrl = new THREE.Vector3(
  (pWorld_default.x + P_default.x) / 2 - 1.0,
  (pWorld_default.y + P_default.y) / 2 + 0.8,
  (pWorld_default.z + P_default.z) / 2 + 0.3
);
createArrowTube(
  pWorld_default.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.1, 0)),
  P_default.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(-0.12, -0.08, 0)),
  arrow1Ctrl, 0.022
);

// Arrow P→p' (sweep from P down to right plane)
const arrow2Ctrl = new THREE.Vector3(
  (P_default.x + pPrime_default_pos.x) / 2 + 0.9,
  (P_default.y + pPrime_default_pos.y) / 2 + 0.5,
  (P_default.z + pPrime_default_pos.z) / 2 + 0.2
);
createArrowTube(
  P_default.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0.12, -0.08, 0)),
  pPrime_default_pos.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.1, 0)),
  arrow2Ctrl, 0.022
);

// Self-loop at P (circular arrow above P)
const loopCenter = P_default.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0.1, 0.4, 0));
const loopRadius = 0.3;
const loopPts = [];
for (let i = 0; i <= 40; i++) {
  const angle = -Math.PI * 0.6 + (i / 40) * Math.PI * 1.7;
  loopPts.push(new THREE.Vector3(
    loopCenter.x + loopRadius * Math.cos(angle),
    loopCenter.y + loopRadius * Math.sin(angle),
    loopCenter.z
  ));
}
const loopCurve = new THREE.CatmullRomCurve3(loopPts);
const loopTube = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.TubeGeometry(loopCurve, 40, 0.022, 8, false), grayMat);
scene.add(loopTube);
const loopEnd = loopPts[loopPts.length - 1];
const loopTangent = loopPts[loopPts.length - 1].clone().sub(loopPts[loopPts.length - 2]).normalize();
const loopCone = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.ConeGeometry(0.06, 0.16, 8), grayMat);
loopCone.position.copy(loopEnd);
loopCone.quaternion.setFromUnitVectors(new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0), loopTangent);
scene.add(loopCone);

// Baseline arrow C₂→C₁ (curved below)
const baseCtrl = new THREE.Vector3(0, -1.0, 0);
createArrowTube(
  C2.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0.15, -0.15, 0)),
  C1.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(-0.15, -0.15, 0)),
  baseCtrl, 0.022
);

// ── Update function ──
const depthSlider = document.getElementById('depthZ');
const rotSlider = document.getElementById('rotY');
const transSlider = document.getElementById('transX');

function updateScene() {
  const z = parseFloat(depthSlider.value);
  const rotYDeg = parseFloat(rotSlider.value);
  const transXVal = parseFloat(transSlider.value);
  const rotYRad = rotYDeg * Math.PI / 180;

  // Back-project p to get P in target camera coords
  const P_cam2 = new THREE.Vector3(z * p_img.x / f, z * p_img.y / f, z);

  // P in world coords
  const P_world = C2.clone()
    .add(cam2.X.clone().multiplyScalar(P_cam2.x))
    .add(cam2.Y.clone().multiplyScalar(P_cam2.y))
    .add(cam2.Z.clone().multiplyScalar(P_cam2.z));

  // p on target plane (fixed)
  const p_on_plane = C2.clone()
    .add(cam2.X.clone().multiplyScalar(p_img.x / f))
    .add(cam2.Y.clone().multiplyScalar(p_img.y / f))
    .add(cam2.Z.clone().multiplyScalar(1.0));

  // Modified reference camera
  const cosR = Math.cos(rotYRad), sinR = Math.sin(rotYRad);
  const C1_mod = C1.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(transXVal, 0, 0));
  const X1_mod = new THREE.Vector3(
    cam1.X.x * cosR + cam1.X.z * sinR,
    cam1.X.y,
    -cam1.X.x * sinR + cam1.X.z * cosR
  );
  const Y1_mod = new THREE.Vector3(
    cam1.Y.x * cosR + cam1.Y.z * sinR,
    cam1.Y.y,
    -cam1.Y.x * sinR + cam1.Y.z * cosR
  );
  const Z1_mod = new THREE.Vector3(
    cam1.Z.x * cosR + cam1.Z.z * sinR,
    cam1.Z.y,
    -cam1.Z.x * sinR + cam1.Z.z * cosR
  );

  // Project P into modified reference camera
  const P_rel = P_world.clone().sub(C1_mod);
  const P_ref = new THREE.Vector3(
    X1_mod.dot(P_rel),
    Y1_mod.dot(P_rel),
    Z1_mod.dot(P_rel)
  );

  let pPrimeVisible = false;
  let pPrime_world = new THREE.Vector3();

  if (P_ref.z > 0.05) {
    const pPrime_img = { x: f * P_ref.x / P_ref.z, y: f * P_ref.y / P_ref.z };
    if (Math.abs(pPrime_img.x) < 1.2 && Math.abs(pPrime_img.y) < 1.0) {
      pPrime_world = C1_mod.clone()
        .add(X1_mod.clone().multiplyScalar(pPrime_img.x / f))
        .add(Y1_mod.clone().multiplyScalar(pPrime_img.y / f))
        .add(Z1_mod.clone().multiplyScalar(1.0));
      pPrimeVisible = true;
    }
  }

  // Update P position
  pMesh.position.copy(P_world);

  // Update p position (fixed)
  pDot.position.copy(p_on_plane);

  // Update p' position
  if (pPrimeVisible) {
    pPrimeDot.visible = true;
    pPrimeDot.position.copy(pPrime_world);
  } else {
    pPrimeDot.visible = false;
  }

  // Update dashed ray from C₂ through p to P
  const ray2Pts = [C2.clone(), p_on_plane.clone(), P_world.clone()];
  ray2.geometry.dispose();
  ray2.geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry().setFromPoints(ray2Pts);
  ray2.computeLineDistances();

  // Update dashed ray from C₁ through p' to P
  if (pPrimeVisible) {
    ray1.visible = true;
    const ray1Pts = [C1_mod.clone(), pPrime_world.clone(), P_world.clone()];
    ray1.geometry.dispose();
    ray1.geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry().setFromPoints(ray1Pts);
    ray1.computeLineDistances();
  } else {
    ray1.visible = false;
  }

  // Update reference plane and camera center positions if translated/rotated
  c1Mesh.position.copy(C1_mod);
  const m1 = new THREE.Matrix4().makeBasis(X1_mod, Y1_mod, Z1_mod);
  plane1.quaternion.setFromRotationMatrix(m1);
  plane1.position.copy(C1_mod).add(Z1_mod.clone().multiplyScalar(1.0));
}

depthSlider.addEventListener('input', updateScene);
rotSlider.addEventListener('input', updateScene);
transSlider.addEventListener('input', updateScene);

// ── Demo steps ──
const steps = [
  { depthZ: 4, rotY: 0, transX: 0 },
  { depthZ: 7, rotY: 0, transX: 0 },
  { depthZ: 4, rotY: 25, transX: 1 }
];

let tweenId = null;
function goToStep(idx) {
  const target = steps[idx];
  const start = {
    depthZ: parseFloat(depthSlider.value),
    rotY: parseFloat(rotSlider.value),
    transX: parseFloat(transSlider.value)
  };
  const duration = 800;
  const t0 = performance.now();
  if (tweenId) cancelAnimationFrame(tweenId);
  function tick() {
    const t = Math.min(1, (performance.now() - t0) / duration);
    const ease = t * t * (3 - 2 * t);
    depthSlider.value = start.depthZ + (target.depthZ - start.depthZ) * ease;
    rotSlider.value = start.rotY + (target.rotY - start.rotY) * ease;
    transSlider.value = start.transX + (target.transX - start.transX) * ease;
    updateScene();
    if (t < 1) tweenId = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  }
  tick();
}

document.getElementById('btnStep0').addEventListener('click', () => goToStep(0));
document.getElementById('btnStep1').addEventListener('click', () => goToStep(1));
document.getElementById('btnStep2').addEventListener('click', () => goToStep(2));

// ── Initial update ──
updateScene();

// ── Camera view: near-frontal to match source diagram composition ──
setCameraView({
  projection: 'perspective',
  azimuthDeg: 12,
  elevationDeg: 8,
  rollDeg: 0,
  heightFraction: 0.72
});

// ── Labels ─
addLabel('ℓ<sub>2</sub>', new THREE.Vector3(-1.6, -0.2, 1.15), { fontSize: '18px', bold: true });
addLabel('ℓ<sub>1</sub>', new THREE.Vector3(1.8, -0.2, 1.15), { fontSize: '18px', bold: true });
addLabel('p', pWorld_default.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(-0.15, 0.12, 0)), { fontSize: '15px', bold: true });
addLabel("p'", pPrime_default_pos.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0.15, -0.12, 0)), { fontSize: '15px', bold: true });
addLabel('P', P_default.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(-0.18, 0.14, 0)), { fontSize: '16px', bold: true });
addLabel('P=zK<sup>-1</sup>p', new THREE.Vector3(-1.3, 1.7, 2.2), { fontSize: '14px', bold: true });
addLabel("P'=MP", P_default.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0.4, 0.5, 0)), { fontSize: '14px', bold: true });
addLabel("p'=KP", new THREE.Vector3(1.5, 1.4, 2.0), { fontSize: '14px', bold: true });
addLabel('R, T', new THREE.Vector3(0, -1.2, 0), { fontSize: '15px', bold: true });
addLabel('Target frame', new THREE.Vector3(-2.4, -0.6, 0), { fontSize: '16px' });
addLabel('Reference frame', new THREE.Vector3(2.4, -0.6, 0), { fontSize: '16px' });

// ── Interactive elements ──
registerInteractive(pMesh, {
  title: '3D Scene Point P',
  body: 'P is the 3D point reconstructed by back-projecting the image point p using depth z and the intrinsic matrix K: P = zK⁻¹p. Both cameras observe this same point.',
  tooltip: '3D point P = zK⁻¹p'
});

registerInteractive(pDot, {
  title: 'Image point p (target frame)',
  body: 'The image point p on the target image plane ℓ₂. Back-projection through the camera center C₂ gives the ray along which P lies.',
  tooltip: 'Image point p on ℓ₂'
});

registerInteractive(pPrimeDot, {
  title: "Image point p' (reference frame)",
  body: "The projected image point p' = KP' on the reference plane ℓ₁. Its position depends on the relative pose (R, T) and the depth z.",
  tooltip: "Image point p' on ℓ₁"
});

registerInteractive(c2Mesh, {
  title: 'Target camera center C₂',
  body: 'The optical center of the target (left) camera. The back-projection ray from C₂ through p defines the line of sight to P.',
  tooltip: 'Target camera C₂'
});

registerInteractive(c1Mesh, {
  title: 'Reference camera center C₁',
  body: 'The optical center of the reference (right) camera. The projection ray from C₁ through p\' confirms the 3D location of P.',
  tooltip: 'Reference camera C₁'
});
// @FIGURE_CODE_END

// Compute camera bases
function computeBasis(camPos, target) {
  const fwd = target.clone().sub(camPos).normalize();
  const worldUp = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0);
  const right = new THREE.Vector3().crossVectors(worldUp, fwd).normalize();
